chapter_theme: The three instruments (முக்கரணம்): as one man appears in three roles, so the difference of Siva, the Supreme and the soul may be called one; and when Om, breath and space are raised and the stupor of the three instruments is cleared, Nandi gives the inner samadhi of unmani.

2485.reading: As one man, joined to three places, is seen in a different form as each duty requires, so the difference among Siva, the Supreme and the soul, spoken of together, may be called one.
2485.nuance: The image is one person in three roles. ஒன்றெனலாம், 'may be called one', is guarded: it allows the difference while naming it one.

2486.reading: Make the light shine and raise it as Om, make the breath breath and draw it in fittingly, make space space and set it rising upward, and as clarity grows, Siva's state grows clear.
2486.nuance: Each line doubles its noun (ஒளியை ஒளிசெய்து, வளியை வளிசெய்து, வெளியை வெளிசெய்து), so each is made purely itself. The three are traditionally taken as the mantra, the breath and the inner space of the yogic practice.

2487.reading: Nandi gave, as a thing held in the hand, what comes when the stupor of the three instruments is cleared; great Manonmani then goes on alone, and that unmani is the inner samadhi.
2487.nuance: முக்கரணம் are traditionally mind, speech and body, or the inner instruments. மனோன்மணி is a name of Shakti and a stage of yoga; உன்மணி (unmani) is the state beyond the mind. அக்கைக்காரணம் is obscure.

source_issues: 2487 line 2 (அக்கைக்காரணம்) is obscure and may be corrupt.
